questions.question: According to the PZO paper, how does film thickness produce competing effects on energy-storage performance?
questions.supporting_excerpt: Ultrathin ﬁlms possess low energy loss (Wloss), the dielectric constant and Ps increase as the ﬁlm thickness increases. However, excessively thick ﬁlms suffer from low energy storage efﬁciency and susceptibility to breakdown, which impair the energy storage performance
questions.reference_answer: Increasing thickness can raise dielectric constant and Ps, but excessively thick films can reduce efficiency and increase breakdown susceptibility.

questions.question: How does the perturbation model overcome previous constant-coefficient or isotropic approximations?
questions.supporting_excerpt: Through a Fou- rier-space perturbation scheme, we achieve the ability to treat the full anisotropic gradient energy tensor with spatial variations, overcoming limitations of previous constant-coeﬃ- cient or isotropic approximations.
questions.reference_answer: The Fourier-space perturbation formulation treats a full anisotropic gradient-energy tensor whose coefficients vary spatially.

questions.question: According to the abstract, how do tensile strain and defect dipoles jointly affect PZO-based antiferroelectric films?
questions.supporting_excerpt: applying tensile strain to the ﬁlms can effectively increase the transition electric ﬁeld from antiferroelectric to ferroelectric. In addition, the introduction of defect dipoles while applying tensile strain can signi ﬁcantly reduce the hysteresis and improve energy storage ef ﬁciency.
questions.reference_answer: Tensile strain increases the AFE-to-FE transition field, while defect dipoles combined with tensile strain reduce hysteresis and improve efficiency.
